summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of Crohn’s disease status post subtotal colectomy and ileorectal anastomosis, steroid-dependent and refractory to multiple biologics, was admitted for abdominal pain and increased liquid stool output consistent with a disease flare. He had self-increased his prednisone dose and presented with right-sided flank pain, raising concern for nephrolithiasis. Imaging showed no obstruction but revealed a nonobstructing 7mm right renal stone. He was treated with IV steroids, bowel rest, IV fluids, and pain management. His symptoms improved, with decreased stool frequency and pain. He transitioned to oral prednisone, oxycodone, and hydrocortisone enemas. His paresthesias resolved, and he received his monthly B12 injection. He was discharged home with a plan to follow up with gastroenterology, continuing steroid taper, and monitoring for stone passage.
problems: Regional enteritis of small intestine with large intestine
